title: More Ways to Trade: Institutional Execution Through BitGo Global Markets
summary: Access market and limit orders, algorithmic execution strategies, RFQ, and OTC trading through BitGo's institutional markets offering.
body_markdown:
## Key Takeaways


-


**More ways to execute through BitGo Global Markets.** Access market and limit orders, algorithmic execution strategies, RFQ, and OTC trading through BitGo's institutional markets offering.


-


**Get price certainty for larger trades.** RFQ enables eligible clients to request and review a firm price before committing to execution, providing an alternative to sweeping available liquidity.


-


**Access liquidity beyond BitGo's trading platform.** Through Go Network Off-Exchange Settlement (OES), eligible institutions can trade on supported exchanges and ECNs while keeping assets in BitGo qualified custody, with settlement through BitGo.


Institutional trading requires flexibility. Some trades call for immediate execution, others benefit from strategies that manage execution over time, and larger orders may require a firm price before committing.


Through[BitGo Global Markets](https://www.bitgo.com/global-markets/?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=trading&utm_campaign=executionoptions) , institutions can access multiple execution methods, institutional liquidity, and experienced trading professionals, supported by BitGo's broader custody and settlement infrastructure.


With the addition of request for quote (RFQ) functionality, eligible clients have another way to execute larger trades alongside existing electronic and OTC trading capabilities.


## Electronic trading: Execute on your terms


[BitGo's electronic trading capabilities](https://www.bitgo.com/products/electronic-trading/?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=trading&utm_campaign=executionoptions) give institutions access to aggregated liquidity through a range of order types and execution strategies.


Clients can choose from:


-


**Market orders:** Execute at available market prices when immediacy is the priority.


-


**Limit orders:** Set a specified price or better, giving clients greater control over execution price.


-


**TWAP (Time-Weighted Average Price):** Spread execution over a defined period to reduce reliance on a single point-in-time price.


-


**Steady Pace:** Execute orders incrementally using a paced execution strategy.


-


**Stop orders:** Trigger an order when a specified price condition is reached.


These methods give institutions the flexibility to approach trades based on their size, timing, and execution objectives.


## RFQ: Request a firm price before executing


For larger trades, institutions may want greater price certainty before committing to a transaction. With RFQ, eligible clients can request a firm quote for a specified trade size and review the price before deciding whether to execute.


Rather than immediately sweeping available liquidity across multiple venues, RFQ provides an alternative workflow in which clients can evaluate a quoted price before confirming the trade. This gives institutions another execution option for block-sized orders, alongside existing market and algorithmic order types.


## OTC trading: Access tailored execution and liquidity


For institutions with larger or more complex trading requirements, BitGo Global Markets also offers dedicated[OTC voice and chat](https://www.bitgo.com/products/otc-trading/?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=trading&utm_campaign=executionoptions) execution, providing direct access to experienced traders and institutional liquidity. Through BitGo's institutional OTC trading capabilities, clients can request pricing directly from the desk and access execution support for[block trades](https://www.bitgo.com/resources/blog/regulated-otc-institutional-otc-desks-and-crypto-block-trades/?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=trading&utm_campaign=executionoptions) and strategies that may require a more tailored approach.


Together, electronic order types, RFQ, and dedicated OTC voice and chat execution give clients a range of trading workflows based on their objectives, order size, and execution preferences.


## Access trading through the workflows you already use


Execution choice also extends to how institutions connect with BitGo. Clients can place and manage trades through the BitGo interface or integrate trading into existing systems using supported[API](https://developers.bitgo.com/?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=trading&utm_campaign=executionoptions) or OEMS connectivity.


For trading firms and institutions with automated workflows, programmatic access enables order submission, monitoring, and execution without requiring teams to manage each trade manually. Whether trading directly through the interface or integrating with an existing trading system, clients can access BitGo's execution capabilities through the workflows that fit their operations.


## Connected to BitGo's institutional infrastructure


Execution is one part of the institutional trading lifecycle. Institutions also need to manage assets, move liquidity, and settle transactions efficiently. BitGo Global Markets connects institutional execution with BitGo's broader digital asset infrastructure, including[qualified custody](https://www.bitgo.com/products/qualified-custody/?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=trading&utm_campaign=executionoptions) and Go Network settlement services.


Through[Go Network Off-Exchange Settlement (OES)](https://www.bitgo.com/products/go-network-oes/?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=trading&utm_campaign=executionoptions) capabilities, eligible institutions can access liquidity on support exchanges, including[OKX](https://www.bitgo.com/resources/blog/okx-to-join-bitgos-go-network/?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=trading&utm_campaign=executionoptions) , and electronic communication networks (ECNs), such as[Crossover Markets](https://www.bitgo.com/resources/blog/bitgo-and-crossover-markets-surpass-2-billion-in-cleared-volume/?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=trading&utm_campaign=executionoptions) ’ CROSSx, while keeping assets in BitGo qualified custody. Go Network also supports[delivery-vs-payment (DvP)](https://www.bitgo.com/products/go-network-dvp/?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=trading&utm_campaign=executionoptions) settlement, enabling eligible counterparties to exchange assets for coordinated settlement.


Together, these capabilities help institutions coordinate trading, custody, and settlement through BitGo.


## One relationship. More ways to trade.


From electronic order types and algorithmic strategies to RFQ and dedicated OTC execution, BitGo Global Markets gives institutions multiple ways to access liquidity and execute trades based on their objectives.


And execution is only part of the offering. Global Markets also brings together Prime Financing, derivatives and structured solutions, collateral management, research, and asset management, supported by BitGo's broader institutional infrastructure.


Whether you're looking to execute a large trade, explore different execution strategies, or access additional financial solutions, our experienced capital markets team can help you evaluate the options available to your institution.


[Contact the BitGo team](https://calendly.com/d/crmk-p2t-k78?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=trading&utm_campaign=executionoptions) to discuss your trading objectives.


## Frequently Asked Questions


### What execution methods does BitGo support?


BitGo offers electronic trading through market, limit, and supported algorithmic order types, as well as RFQ and OTC execution capabilities. Availability may vary by client, entity, and integration.


### How is RFQ different from a market order?


A market order seeks execution at available market prices. RFQ allows clients to request and review a firm quote for a specified trade size before deciding whether to execute.


### Does RFQ replace existing execution methods?


No. RFQ expands the execution options available through BitGo Trade. Clients can continue using supported electronic order types based on their trading requirements.


### Can institutions integrate trading into their own systems?


Yes. BitGo supports programmatic trading connectivity, enabling eligible institutions to integrate order submission and execution workflows into their existing systems.


### How does BitGo connect trading with custody and settlement?


BitGo offers qualified custody and settlement capabilities alongside its institutional trading services. Eligible clients can also access Go Network settlement solutions, depending on their trading and operational setup.


### How does institutional trading fit into BitGo Global Markets?


Institutional execution is a core offering within BitGo Global Markets, which brings together electronic trading, OTC voice and chat execution, Prime Financing, derivatives and structured solutions, collateral management, research, and asset management. These capabilities are supported by BitGo's broader custody and settlement infrastructure.
